data.narrative:
Helical Fusion is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Takaya Taguchi and Junichi Miyazawa that has raised $98M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Nuclear Energy sector comp universe of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Aalo Atomics.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using the $98M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $186M. A peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow nuclear energy subset—only one adjacent-stage peer emerged from filtered screening, falling below the three-datapoint threshold needed for statistical reliability.

The triangulated valuation range is $158M (low) to $214M (high), with $186M as the median. This single-method analysis carries meaningful uncertainty inherent to a sparse-peer environment and reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than comparable transaction multiples. The primary sensitivities are the appropriateness of the 1.9x multiplier for Helical Fusion's specific technical and capital profile, and the degree to which broader sector comps (if included) would shift the implied range. Additional diligence on unit economics and technology differentiation would be warranted before finalizing.
